problem_type: Performance benchmark verdict and process status divergence
symptom: The canvas benchmark could write a result with pass:false while its process still exited successfully, allowing an outer canvas suite or CI job to report PASS.
direct_cause: The benchmark calculated and persisted results.pass but never projected that verdict onto process.exitCode, and no isolated verdict test covered the process boundary.
class_root: Recorded performance evidence and executable gate status had no shared fail-closed verdict boundary.
affected_population: Warmup failures and unreliable benchmark runs
Local, CI, and release callers that rely on the benchmark exit status
internal_only_reason: This is an internal Node process contract between Nomi's own JSON verdict and its caller-visible exit status; no third-party behavior decides the invariant.
invariants: Only an explicit results.pass === true may exit successfully.
Warmup, hard failure, and budget failure evidence remains persisted before the nonzero exit status is applied.
Every caller observes the same verdict through the benchmark process status.
generality_proof: Direct CLI, canvas-real-suite, system profile, CI, and release callers all spawn the same benchmark process. Projecting the persisted verdict at that process boundary covers every caller without scenario-specific checks.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Convert the persisted benchmark pass contract into a fail-closed process exit status for every caller.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The benchmark applies the shared verdict only after its final JSON result has been written.
The suite already treats any nonzero child status as failure, so the shared process verdict propagates without another interpretation.

recurrence.reason: Any future budget or scenario failure could produce pass:false again, and every wrapper would continue trusting exit status.
same_class_scan: Searched the benchmark for results.pass, writeResults, process.exit, process.exitCode, verdict, warmupFailures, and budgetChecks.
Inspected canvas-real-suite and test-system stage execution; both classify the child solely from its process status.
Inspected tracked canvas performance evidence and confirmed pass is a first-class persisted field consumed by maintainers.

prevention.invariant: A benchmark process can report success only when its final persisted result explicitly reports pass:true.
prevention.failure_mode: False, missing, or malformed pass state sets process.exitCode to 1 after evidence is written.
prevention.strategy: Introduce one testable verdict adapter and require the benchmark CLI to use it after final result persistence.

legacy_paths.rationale: There is one benchmark executable; its missing exit projection is completed in place and no alternate caller or fallback verdict path exists.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The missing invariant is repository-owned process status handling and does not depend on Electron, Playwright, or Node version behavior.

migration: No stored data migration is required. Existing JSON evidence remains readable; future runs additionally expose the same pass field through process status.
residual_risks: Machine-to-machine performance variance remains possible; the benchmark records machine identity and detailed metric evidence so a failure is diagnosed rather than silently accepted.
